claim_verbatim: The ₹7,280 crore scheme for 6,000 tonnes a year drew 20 bids by August 2026. By mid-October, no winner had been named, and no Indian sintered magnet will come off a line before late 2028.
context: Part of the argument that India's plan to make rare-earth magnets at home is slower than a cheap reserve; China's pause on wider rare-earth export controls runs out on 10 November 2026.
source: Substack essay 'Sovereign Black Warrant: India’s Existential Material Trap' (also posted as an X article, https://x.com/ctindale/status/2109474636299903295)
resolution_criterion: TRUE if no sintered NdFeB rare-earth permanent magnet comes off a commercial production line in India (including any line under the ₹7,280 crore REPM scheme) before 1 October 2028. FALSE if PIB, company filings or major press report commercial output of Indian-made sintered NdFeB magnets before that date. Pilot, R&D or lab output does not count. 'Late 2028' is read as Q4 2028, so the window closes 30 Sep 2028.
resolution_rule_fixed: TRUE if no sintered NdFeB rare-earth permanent magnet comes off a commercial production line in India (including any line under the ₹7,280 crore REPM scheme) before 1 October 2028. FALSE if PIB, company filings or major press report commercial output of Indian-made sintered NdFeB magnets before that date. Pilot, R&D or lab output does not count. 'Late 2028' is read as Q4 2028, so the window closes 30 Sep 2028.
resolution_source_planned: PIB / Ministry of Heavy Industries releases on the REPM scheme; awardee company filings; Economic Times, Business Standard, Reuters
mechanism: Scheme award still pending in mid-October 2026 and magnet plants take years to build and qualify, so domestic sintered output cannot start before late 2028.
notes: Scope fixed to sintered NdFeB on a commercial line, because that is what the scheme he cites funds. Possible conflict to check, not verified this run: IREL has been reported to run a samarium-cobalt magnet plant at Visakhapatnam; SmCo strategic output is outside this rule, and that choice is flagged here rather than made silently. Inferred 0.90 from 'will'; queued for Craig to confirm.

claim_verbatim: I count an internal deficit of 181 GW between module assembly and domestic cell production. An embargo would leave those empty glass sheds cold within weeks.
context: Indian solar: 213 GW of module capacity against 32 GW of domestic cell capacity by August 2026.
source: Substack essay 'Sovereign Black Warrant: India’s Existential Material Trap' (also posted as an X article, https://x.com/ctindale/status/2109474636299903295)
resolution_criterion: Not a crisp yes/no: conditional on a Chinese embargo with no defined trigger or date; unscorable as written unless an embargo occurs and is defined.
resolution_rule_fixed: Not a crisp yes/no: conditional on a Chinese embargo with no defined trigger or date; unscorable as written unless an embargo occurs and is defined.
resolution_source_planned: Indian solar module output data (MNRE, industry bodies) after any Chinese cell/wafer export ban
mechanism: Indian module plants depend on imported Chinese cells and wafers and hold little stock.
notes: Conditional call. Logged as unscorable; if China imposes a cell or wafer embargo on India, it can be scored by a new superseding line with the trigger date fixed then.

claim_verbatim: In February 2020 the ratings agency ICRA put formulation makers’ average inventory at 1.5 to 2.5 months. Ten weeks of chemical stock will not outlast an embargo.
context: Indian pharmaceutical formulators depend on Chinese precursors and active ingredients.
source: Substack essay 'Sovereign Black Warrant: India’s Existential Material Trap' (also posted as an X article, https://x.com/ctindale/status/2109474636299903295)
resolution_criterion: Not a crisp yes/no: conditional on an embargo of undefined scope and length; unscorable as written.
resolution_rule_fixed: Not a crisp yes/no: conditional on an embargo of undefined scope and length; unscorable as written.
resolution_source_planned: Indian drug-formulation output and shortage reports after any Chinese API/KSM export ban
mechanism: Formulation plants hold roughly ten weeks of Chinese precursors, so any embargo longer than that empties production.
notes: Conditional call. Logged as unscorable, same treatment as pl-077.

claim_verbatim: In 1991, a shortage of dollars sent India’s gold to London. The next shortage will be of things dollars cannot buy.
context: Closing argument: India's US$700bn+ reserve cannot buy materials a Chinese licensing office refuses to release.
source: Substack essay 'Sovereign Black Warrant: India’s Existential Material Trap' (also posted as an X article, https://x.com/ctindale/status/2109474636299903295)
resolution_criterion: Not a crisp yes/no: no deadline and no measurable definition of 'the next shortage'; unscorable as written.
resolution_rule_fixed: Not a crisp yes/no: no deadline and no measurable definition of 'the next shortage'; unscorable as written.
mechanism: Chinese export licensing, not price or foreign exchange, controls India's access to critical inputs.
notes: Logged as unscorable: no deadline or threshold.
